title.en: The Axis Invasion and the Triple Occupation

summary.en: German forces invaded on 6 April 1941 after the Italian attack from Albania had failed. Athens fell on 27 April and Crete followed in May. The country was then divided into German, Italian and Bulgarian zones of occupation while the Greek state continued to exist in exile, which is why the map shows occupation as a layer over sovereignty rather than in place of it.

body_html.en:
The German attack came through Bulgaria against the Metaxas Line and through Yugoslavia behind it. Thessaloniki fell on 9 April, the army in Albania was cut off and surrendered on 20 April, and the swastika flew on the Acropolis on 27 April. The king and government withdrew to Crete and then, after the airborne invasion of May, to Cairo.

The occupiers divided the country. Germany kept Athens, central Macedonia, the strategic islands and most of Crete; Bulgaria annexed in all but name eastern Macedonia and western Thrace; Italy took the rest. The famine of the winter of 1941 to 1942 killed tens of thousands in Athens alone.

sources.title: Inside Hitler's Greece: The Experience of Occupation, 1941-44
sources.author: Mark Mazower
